# Composer

A chat message box: text that grows from one line as the person writes, a send button, and room for the rest of a composer, in one frame with one focus outline. Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line, or `sendOn="mod-enter"` for Ctrl+Enter, and Enter never sends mid-word in an input method. `actions` holds the buttons before Send (emoji, attach, formatting), `toolbar` a formatting bar above the text while it is on, and `attachments` the files waiting to go. `sendDisabledReason` turns sending off and says why, while the person can still write, and `highlights` marks words in the text, as TextArea's do.

```tsx
import { Composer } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/composer/composer";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Composer label="Message Mia" placeholder="Write a message" onSend={(text) => send(text)} />
<Composer
  label="Reply"
  value={text}
  onValueChange={setText}
  onSend={(text) => { send(text); setText(""); }}
  highlights={[{ start: 0, end: 22, label: "Suggested by your assistant" }]}
  description="Your assistant's suggestions are underlined."
  actions={<Button variant="plain" aria-label="Attach a file" onClick={attach}><PaperclipIcon /></Button>}
  attachments={files.length > 0 && files.map((file) => <Attachment key={file.name} name={file.name} onRemove={() => remove(file)} />)}
  sendDisabledReason={offline ? "You're offline. Sending resumes when you reconnect." : undefined}
/>
```

## Usage

The text is plain text, so emoji from an image catalogue go in as `:shortcode:` tokens: an `Autocomplete` trigger with `catalogue` inserts them as the person types `:` and a few letters, and an `EmojiPicker` with `catalogue` in `actions` gives its `selection.token` to put at the caret. `EmojiText` draws the tokens as the catalogue's images once the message is sent. Given the `catalogue` too, Composer puts an emoji typed from the system's emoji panel or pasted in as its token as well.

## Use instead when

- Use `TextArea` instead for a long text that is saved rather than sent, and `Message` for a message once it is sent.

## Props

Type: `ComposerProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons before the send button: emoji, attach a file, show formatting. Ouro `Button`s with `variant="plain"` and an `aria-label`. |
| `attachments` | `ReactNode` |  | Files waiting to go with the message, shown in a row inside the box under the text: `Attachment` items with `onRemove`. Pass it only when there are some; with it, the message can be sent without text. |
| `attachmentsLabel` | `string` | `"Attachments"` | A name for the attachments row, for screen readers. |
| `catalogue` | `EmojiCatalogue` |  | An image emoji catalogue. With it, an emoji typed into the box (from the system's emoji panel, say) or pasted goes in as its `:shortcode:` token, the token `Autocomplete` and `EmojiPicker` insert, so the text holds the catalogue's emoji only as tokens, which `EmojiText` draws as its images. That includes an emoji joined from others and one with a skin tone, which become the catalogue's emoji or tone for it; an emoji the catalogue does not list stays as it is. The caret lands after what went in, and one undo takes it out. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-2`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The starting text, for an uncontrolled composer, which clears itself after a send. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | A quiet line under the box, read as the text's description: what the marks mean, a character count. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the whole composer: the box and the send button. |
| `highlights` | `readonly TextAreaHighlight[]` |  | Ranges of the text to mark in place, as TextArea's `highlights`: words an assistant suggested, spelling notes. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the message box is for, read as its name: "Message Mia", "Reply in thread". Required: the box shows `placeholder`, which is not a label. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `10` | Lines it grows to before it scrolls. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The form field name the text submits under. |
| `onHighlightsChange` | `((highlights: TextAreaHighlight[]) => void)` |  | Called with the highlights moved to fit the text after the person edits it, as TextArea's. |
| `onSend` (required) | `(text: string, event: ComposerSendEvent) => void` |  | Called with the text when the person sends: Enter in the box (see `sendOn`) or the send button. The event says which, and `event.isTrusted` that a person did it. It is not called while the text is blank (unless there are `attachments`), while `sending`, or with `sendDisabledReason` set. Without `value`, the box clears after it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the new text when it changes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | An example of what to write, shown on the first line while the box is empty. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>` |  | The `<textarea>`. |
| `rows` | `number` | `1` | Lines the box starts with; it grows as the person writes. |
| `sendDisabledReason` | `string` |  | Sending is off, and why: "Sending is off while you review the draft". The person can still write; the send button is disabled, the reason shows under the box and is read with it, and pressing Enter says it again. |
| `sending` | `boolean` |  | The message is on its way: the send button shows a spinner, and nothing more sends until it is done. |
| `sendingLabel` | `string` | `"Sending"` | What screen readers hear when `sending` turns on. |
| `sendLabel` | `string` | `"Send"` | The send button's name, which its tooltip shows too. |
| `sendOn` | `"enter" \| "mod-enter"` | `"enter"` | Which key sends. `enter`: Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line, as chat apps do. `mod-enter`: Ctrl+Enter (Command+Enter on a Mac) sends and Enter starts a new line, for long messages. Enter never sends while an input method is composing a word. |
| `toolbar` | `ReactNode` |  | Tools shown above the text, inside the box: a formatting bar. Pass it only while it should show, as when the person turns formatting on. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The text, for a controlled composer; pair it with `onValueChange`, and clear it yourself once the message is sent. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` and `TextareaHTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `enterToSend`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `sendOn`: `<Composer sendOn="mod-enter">`.
- `loading`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `sending`: `<Composer sending>`.
- `onSubmit`: Not a prop. Sending calls `onSend`: `<Composer onSend={(text) => send(text)}>`.
- `sendDisabled`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `sendDisabledReason`: `<Composer sendDisabledReason="Sending is off">`.
- `submitOnEnter`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `sendOn`: `<Composer sendOn="mod-enter">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `ComposerSendEvent`

What sent the message: the Enter key in the box, or a press of the send button.

```ts
type ComposerSendEvent = KeyboardEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement> | MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>;
```

### `EmojiCatalogue`

An image-based emoji set, by category: what `EmojiPicker`, `ReactionBar`, `Autocomplete` and `EmojiText` draw instead of the platform's emoji font when an app passes it. Put an organization's custom emoji in a category of their own, labelled by the app. The image addresses are used as they are, so an app that loads images its own way (a content security policy, a custom scheme, signed or `blob:` URLs) puts the addresses it can load in the catalogue when it builds it.

```ts
interface EmojiCatalogue {
  /** The categories, in the order they show. An emoji in more than one counts once, by its id. */
  categories: readonly EmojiCatalogueCategory[];
}
```

### `EmojiCatalogueCategory`

A category of a catalogue: its name, the icon its button shows, and its emoji in order.

```ts
interface EmojiCatalogueCategory {
  /** Identifies the category, unique in the catalogue: `"people"`, `"custom"`. */
  id: string;
  /** Its name, shown as its heading and read for its button: `"People"`, or the organization's name for its custom emoji. */
  label: string;
  /** What its button in a picker's category bar shows: an icon element. Defaults to its first emoji's image. */
  icon?: ReactNode;
  /** Its emoji, in the order they show. */
  items: readonly EmojiItem[];
}
```

### `EmojiFilmstrip`

An animation drawn as a filmstrip: square frames stacked top to bottom in one image, so the frames are the image's height over its width.

```ts
interface EmojiFilmstrip {
  /** The filmstrip image's address. */
  src: string;
  /** Frames a second. */
  fps: number;
}
```

### `EmojiItem`

One emoji in an image catalogue: its id, its name and the image that draws it. An app maps its own emoji set to this, whether a standard set or an organization's custom emoji.

```ts
interface EmojiItem {
  /** Identifies the emoji, unique in the catalogue: `"party"`. Reactions, recents and `:id:` tokens use it. */
  id: string;
  /** Its name, which is the image's `alt`, what screen readers hear and what the search matches first: `"Party popper"`. */
  name: string;
  /**
   * The still image's address. It shows whenever the emoji is not playing, and always with reduced motion.
   */
  src: string;
  /** Sizes of the still image for sharper screens, as `<img srcset>`: `"party-2x.png 2x"`. */
  srcSet?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * An animated image (GIF, animated WebP or PNG), which plays while the pointer is on the emoji
   * or on the button around it, or that button has focus. With reduced motion it never plays.
   */
  animatedSrc?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * The animation as a filmstrip, square frames stacked top to bottom in one image, for an
   * emoji without `animatedSrc`: while the emoji plays, it steps through the frames at `fps`;
   * otherwise, and always with reduced motion, `src` shows.
   */
  filmstrip?: EmojiFilmstrip | undefined;
  /** The still image's width in pixels, given to the `<img>` so the page keeps its shape while it loads. It shows at the text's size. */
  width?: number | undefined;
  /** The still image's height in pixels, as `width`. */
  height?: number | undefined;
  /** Short names typed between colons, without them: `["party", "tada"]`. The first makes the emoji's token, `:party:`. */
  shortcodes?: readonly string[] | undefined;
  /** More words the search matches: `["celebrate", "hooray"]`. */
  keywords?: readonly string[] | undefined;
  /**
   * The emoji as plain text, such as its Unicode character (`"🎉"`), for places an image cannot
   * go (a copied message, a notification). `EmojiText` finds it in messages and draws the image;
   * Ouro never draws it as text.
   */
  text?: string | undefined;
  /** It is the organization's or app's own emoji rather than one of the standard set. Ouro draws it the same; apps can label or treat it apart. */
  custom?: boolean | undefined;
  /**
   * The emoji in Unicode's five skin tones, light to dark; leave it out for an emoji without tones.
   */
  skinTones?: readonly EmojiItemTone[] | undefined;
}
```

### `EmojiItemTone`

An emoji's image in one skin tone: `skinTones` on an `EmojiItem`.

```ts
interface EmojiItemTone {
  /** Identifies the emoji in this tone, unique in the catalogue: `"thumbs-up-tone3"`. Reactions and tokens use it. */
  id: string;
  /** The still image's address. */
  src: string;
  /** Sizes of the still image for sharper screens, as `<img srcset>`: `"wave-2x.png 2x"`. */
  srcSet?: string | undefined;
  /** An animated image (GIF, animated WebP or PNG), shown while the emoji plays; the still one shows otherwise. */
  animatedSrc?: string | undefined;
  /** The animation as a filmstrip of square frames, played while the emoji plays, for a tone without `animatedSrc`. */
  filmstrip?: EmojiFilmstrip | undefined;
  /**
   * The emoji in this tone as text (`"👍🏽"`), which `EmojiText` finds in messages; Ouro never draws it as text.
   */
  text?: string | undefined;
}
```

### `TextAreaHighlight`

A range of a TextArea's text that it marks: words an assistant suggested in the person's draft, a possible spelling mistake. `start` and `end` are JavaScript string indexes, and `end` is exclusive, so a mark covers `text.slice(start, end)`.

```ts
interface TextAreaHighlight {
  /** Where the mark starts: the index of its first character in the text. */
  start: number;
  /** Where it ends: the index just after its last character. */
  end: number;
  /**
   * What the mark means, which screen readers hear with the words it marks: "Suggested by
   * your assistant", "Possible spelling mistake". Required, so no mark is shown only to sighted people.
   */
  label: string;
  /**
   * The mark's colour, a theme tone. `destructive` and `warning` draw a wavy underline, as
   * spelling and grammar checkers do; the others a dotted underline on a faint tint.
   * @default "primary"
   */
  tone?: "primary" | "secondary" | "destructive" | "success" | "warning" | (string & { 'danger is "destructive"; accent is "primary"; neutral is "secondary"': never }) | undefined;
  /** Your own id for the mark. An edit inside a mark splits it, and both pieces keep its id. */
  id?: string | undefined;
}
```
